properties.title: Al₂O₃ Abundance · Clementine 1D-CNN (Qiu et al., 2025)
properties.authors: Denggao Qiu, Jianguo Yan, Bin Liu
properties.processing:lineage: Clementine UVVIS DIM Mosaic (5 bands: 415, 750, 900, 950, 1000 nm, 100 m/pixel) combined with OMAT as a 6-element input vector. 1D CNN: two Conv1D layers (32 filters, kernel=2, ReLU), MaxPooling1D (pool=2), Dense(64, ReLU), single linear output. L2 regularization (0.001). Adam optimizer (lr=0.01), max 400 epochs, early stopping (patience=30), z-score normalization. Trained on 49 ground-truth points from Apollo, Luna, and Chang'E missions including Chang'E-6. Al₂O₃ cannot be estimated from classical equation models due to spectral complexity; CNN captures the nonlinear Al₂O₃ spectral signature. R²=0.96+ on training set; LOOCV R²=0.947.
properties.lri:data_use_note: Al₂O₃ is the primary indicator of anorthositic highland crust — the dominant aluminum and calcium source on the Moon. Highest LOOCV R² of the five oxides (0.947). Not derivable from classical equation models; CNN-only product. Bimodal distribution cleanly separates highlands (mode 27.76 wt%) from maria (mode 11.63 wt%). High Al₂O₃ terrains identify anorthosite-rich regions relevant to aluminum resource assessment.
properties.lri:quality_note_short: 1D CNN inversion from Clementine UVVIS, calibrated with Chang'E-6 samples. Highest LOOCV R²=0.947 of the five oxides. Global mean 23.88 wt%. Bimodal: highland mode 27.76 wt%, mare mode 11.63 wt%. Not derivable from classical equation models.
properties.lri:quality_note: Al₂O₃ abundance derived from 1D CNN inversion of Clementine UVVIS 5-band reflectance (Qiu et al. 2025, Communications Earth & Environment). This is a CNN-only product — Al₂O₃ spectral characteristics are too complex for classical equation-based inversion, which is why no prior Clementine-based Al₂O₃ global map exists at this resolution. LOOCV R²=0.947 is the highest of all five oxides, reflecting strong and consistent spectral signatures. Global mean 23.88 wt%; bimodal distribution with modes at 11.63 wt% (maria) and 27.76 wt% (highlands/non-maria). The bimodal separation cleanly reflects the fundamental maria-highland dichotomy: mare basalts are Al₂O₃-poor (dominated by pyroxene and olivine), while highland anorthosites are Al₂O₃-rich (dominated by plagioclase, ideally ~35 wt%). Non-maria mean 25.84 wt% vs. maria mean 13.76 wt%. The lunar south polar region composition shows Al₂O₃ values consistent with non-mare material. Key resource implication: Al₂O₃-rich terrains identify anorthosite-rich regions, which are potential sources of aluminum metal and oxygen through electrolytic reduction of plagioclase.
